Target cells loaded not reported. HTO double-positive exclusion removed cross-sample doublets only; no within-sample doublet call was made, so within-sample residual is unknown.

50,000 cells loaded per channel, 14 donors pooled. That load is beyond the range of the official 10x multiplet tables, so applying the vendor model requires explicit extrapolation -- it may not be extended linearly without stating so. Cross-donor doublets were removed by demuxlet v2 + Vireo; Scrublet score was retained only as a QC covariate.

No loading figure reported and no raw droplet matrix deposited; the per-lane count is a fixed 30,000-barcode whitelist, identical across all 55 lanes, carrying no capture-specific loading information. demuxlet v2 removed cross-donor doublets, so within-donor residual is unknown. Per-lane SNG/DBL/AMB are preserved in liu_demuxlet_per_lane.csv -- they classify the whitelist, which includes empty droplets, and are therefore NOT a doublet rate among real cells.

15,000 cells loaded per sample, protocol-level nominal loading, single donor per capture. No author doublet removal reported, so no upstream depletion to account for. Uncertainty is chemistry: GEO records 3' v3.1 while the paper text describes 5' UMI counting -- unresolved, and the two have different multiplet tables.

Loading is reported cohort-level only (300-14,000 target cells per reaction) and cannot be attached per capture. Our Gate 2 input is demonstrably POST author Scrublet and post manual removal: summing Ncells_manual_removal over the 284 samples gives 1,462,702, matching our per-capture called-cell counts sample by sample. The authors' expected_doublet_rate = 0.08 was their INPUT prior, not a measured removed fraction, so it must not be reused as our residual prior -- and the residual prevalence after their filtering is unknown.

Nominal loading is reported (20,000-30,000 per sample at Newcastle/London; 2 lanes x 25,000 per pool of four at Cambridge) but cannot be mapped to GEM wells. Upstream handling differs by site: Scrublet per sample at Newcastle, emptyDrops plus genotype doublet tagging at Cambridge. Chemistry is also contested (paper 5' NextGEM v1.1 vs SDRF '10xV3').

15,000 cells per array, uniform and stated. A Seq-Well loading-density model exists (Hughes 2020), so this is not 'no model available'; the uncertainty is cross-protocol transfer plus an unknown residual after the authors' heuristic filter (cells with >75 genes per 100 UMIs removed as putative multiplets).
